convertibility_reason: Uses pending stop orders with time-based breakout logic and complex time-window management. Pending order management with multiple cancel/modify conditions makes it more complex than simple indicator-based systems. No external .mqh libraries but the pending order lifecycle and time-filter logic require careful manual conversion.

params.note: SL set as opposite channel side - distance from entry to opposite breakout level
TP set as channel width - same distance as SL from entry

other_exits: Pending orders are cancelled if not triggered within the trading time window
Pending orders are cancelled at end of trading day if not filled
Opposite pending order is deleted when one side triggers

custom_logic_notes: Hans123 breakout strategy: Places buy-stop above the highest high and sell-stop below the lowest low of a configurable lookback period (Periods). Orders are placed at a configurable start time and cancelled at a configurable end time if not triggered. When one side triggers, the opposite pending order is deleted. SL is set at the opposite channel boundary, TP equals SL distance (1:1 RR). Channel width is checked against a minimum threshold to avoid trading in tight ranges. The EA tracks whether a trade was already taken today to prevent re-entry. Time-window parameters (StartTime, EndTime, ClosingTime) control order placement, cancellation, and position closing.
python_conversion_notes: Key challenges: (1) Pending order lifecycle management - placing stop orders, monitoring for fills, cancelling unfilled orders at time window end. (2) Time-filter logic with multiple time windows (start, end, closing). (3) Daily state reset - tracking whether a trade was taken today. (4) SL/TP calculated dynamically from channel boundaries rather than fixed pip values. (5) Must ensure opposite pending order is cancelled when one side fills. (6) Channel high/low calculation uses iHighest/iLowest equivalent over lookback period.
